summary: Backend-only regression run for iter 141 — verified the 3 AI-pipeline / rescan data-integrity fixes. Wrote pytest module test_iter141_rescan_diarize_fixes.py (5 tests, all passing in 95s including a real LLM rescan round-trip). FIX 1 (diarisation now awaited before analyze_meeting) verified via source-code assertions on /app/backend/utils/transcription_pipeline.py — full end-to-end pipeline requires fresh multi-speaker audio which isn't practical here. FIX 2 (uuid-hex mapping ids) and FIX 3 (rescan preserves reviewed items) verified end-to-end against a live meeting (25b5a9be…, analysis 5d0c91ed…): triggered PUT /review/{id}/evidence/{eid} to accept a pending cqc item, then POST /review/{id}/rescan-evidence, polled meetings.rescan_status until 'done', and asserted (a) the accepted item and 5 other pre-existing reviewed items are still present with unchanged status, (b) every freshly-generated mapping across cqc/care_cert/custom carries the new '<prefix>_<12hex>' id, no duplicates, no old 'cqc_1'-style ids. Role-gate check confirms attendee cannot rescan (403).
critical_code_review_comments: FIX 1 is code-verified only. A true regression test needs a fresh multi-speaker recording — worth adding a synthetic 2-speaker fixture (e.g. tiny WAV or a mocked transcribe/diarize) so future refactors can't silently re-parallelise diarisation with analysis without CI catching it.

The _merge() function in review.py preserves *all* non-pending items unconditionally — this is correct per spec but does mean the mappings list can grow unboundedly across repeated rescans. Consider capping or dedupe-by-(ref, status) if this ever becomes an issue in the UI. Not blocking.

seed_data_creation: None. Reused existing in_review meeting 25b5a9be-9f01-4a7d-8f70-9eff81c89bb4 (analysis 5d0c91ed…) in the Test Company org. One pending cqc mapping was flipped to 'accepted' during the test — post-run its status remains 'accepted' (preserved by rescan as designed).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Meeting 25b5a9be-9f01-4a7d-8f70-9eff81c89bb4 (analysis 5d0c91ed-51fa-479d-8e86-9fc9bac306dc) now has a mix of new-style (12-hex uuid) and legacy (sequential 'cqc_1'/'cc_5'/'custom_2') mapping ids after the iter141 rescan — this is expected and intentionally reflects the fix's merge behaviour. If re-running this test suite, note that additional 'accepted' items will accumulate over time; the pytest handles this by picking any current pending item dynamically. Rescan takes ~90s end-to-end via Vertex/OpenAI fallback.
rca of the issue: N/A — all fixes verified working. Original bug (rescan finding more evidence than initial scan) was rooted in analyze_meeting reading an unlabelled transcript because diarisation ran concurrently via asyncio.gather; now diarisation is awaited first (see transcription_pipeline.py lines 328-340) so speaker labels are always present before evidence analysis, closing the gap between initial-scan and rescan quality.
